method: Same owned top-k operator over packed input or admitted utf8 string vector; cached timing includes bulk-admitted cache construction. ASCII fixture gives a known decoded-size bound.
findings: Cached keys improve observed median in eleven of twelve cases; wide-text top-3 at 10000 rows is slower in this run.
At 10000 rows, whole-batch cache incremental tracked peaks range from 1121296 to 21281968 bytes, versus 924 to 5344 for direct reads.
No production default changed; candidate policy needs bounded capacity, concurrency/headroom and broader shape evidence.
limitations: Sequential microbenchmarks, not robust production latency estimates.
Single ASCII column with permutation order; dictionary/null/multiple-key/reuse shapes not covered.
Bulk cache admission models strings/descriptors and one transient view/decoder; native decoder/GC costs remain external.
